material_findings.title: An existing skip-conflicts API parameter is misreported as a missing capability
material_findings.candidate_passage: the reservation API has no parameter matching the GUI’s “Skip conflicting bookings” … PR #1235 … may be closing it
material_findings.original_obligation: O2 governing code facts and O3 accurate issue/fix/evolution chain; O6 API/GUI parity applicability
material_findings.reasoning: Issue #1220 is a user asking for a documented parameter and explicitly considering an undocumented one. The linked merged PR #1235 states the create/update APIs already supported skipping conflicts and adds missing API documentation/examples. The final strengthened the user report into an absent-code claim and treats an already merged documentation change as a possible future behavioral fix. The March 2026 chain therefore supports documentation discoverability, not the asserted missing API semantics. API/GUI parity remains a useful proposed test, but this is a false factual reason for it and affects evaluation of the default booking product. This does not assert that every release has identical behavior: a deployment version is still required.
material_findings.applicability: Applies to the actual final design/claim, with the stated source version and domain conditions; no candidate repair performed.

material_findings.title: The open-checkout index has no specified release path in an immutable event journal
material_findings.candidate_passage: Journals (append-only, never overwrite) … ON custody_events (copy_id) WHERE (event_type = 'checkout' AND returned_at IS NULL)
material_findings.original_obligation: Original ordinary checkout/checkin requirement; P6 normal workflow retained; O2 governing predicate semantics; O5 evidence-backed M5 close-out
material_findings.reasoning: A PostgreSQL partial unique index evaluates the predicate on each indexed row. An immutable checkout event with returned_at NULL remains indexed when a separate checkin event is appended. A later checkout of that copy still collides. The final specifies neither an update that closes the original row nor a separate mutable open-custody projection whose indexed row is removed/closed by checkin. The SQL can work with such a state model, but that model is absent and conflicts with the blanket append-only statement. This is a concrete normal-flow hole in the claimed M5 closure, not a demand for unlimited production detail. The static trace in evidence shows precisely this row-membership problem; no database was run.
material_findings.applicability: Applies to the actual final design/claim, with the stated source version and domain conditions; no candidate repair performed.

material_findings.title: The revised buffer representation is not covered by the stated database backstop
material_findings.candidate_locator: lines 109–111 and 153–169; compare /home/sittingmongoose/PM-Experiments/er11-20261009-116bb1e4/jobs/A-M10-B/control/research/draft.md lines 87–88 and final m15 lines 568–569
material_findings.candidate_passage: buffer_minutes or an explicitly linked blocked range … tstzrange(starts_at, ends_at) WITH && … Back-to-back bookings … never conflict
material_findings.original_obligation: Avoid double booking; O2 enforcement applicability; O5 preservation of buffered conflict semantics through critic m15
material_findings.reasoning: The final allows booking timestamps to be unpadded and buffer_minutes to be stored separately, while its exclusion expression compares only those timestamps. For a booking 10:00–11:00 with 15 minutes cleanup and another starting 11:05, the exclusion sees nonoverlap although the final’s promised booking-plus-buffer conflict check must reject. The alternative linked blocked range is not specified as a row in the constrained relation with an included status; it cannot make the buffer_minutes alternative safe by implication. Application checking may detect many cases, but the final expressly relies on a database backstop to close concurrent check-then-insert races. Critic m15 usefully questioned opaque padding; the changed representation lost the explicit range-enforcement relationship. The finding concerns the allowed representation and claimed backstop, not a claim every separate-block representation is impossible.
material_findings.applicability: Applies to the actual final design/claim, with the stated source version and domain conditions; no candidate repair performed.

material_findings.title: The two-site stock test requires the wrong number of commits
material_findings.candidate_passage: Same consumable stocked at both sites … two sites concurrently consume the last units … exactly one outcome commits (control-row serialization)
material_findings.original_obligation: P2 two-site stock integrity and P6/O6 a meaningful discriminating test with a correct oracle
material_findings.reasoning: The design derives balances per site and locks per (part, site). Locks for A and B are different rows. With one unit physically at each site, one consume at A and one at B are both valid and should both commit without any negative balance. V6’s exactly-one oracle instead rejects that correct implementation; it confuses two contenders for one site balance with two independent site balances. The fixture explicitly begins with stock at both sites. If the intended test were two clients acting on one site’s last unit, it is not the specified V6 fixture. This is a proposed-test error, not a false assertion that the test was executed.
material_findings.applicability: Applies to the actual final design/claim, with the stated source version and domain conditions; no candidate repair performed.

axes.coverage: Complete: O1–O6, members reserving tools, staff consumables/repair/checkout, both sites, unreliable Wi-Fi, low hosting burden, inconsistent historical CSV, double booking, audit and future extension seams.
axes.judgment: The final delivers a self-contained design, unfamiliar product choices, three issue/release chains, explicit P1–P6 dispositions and proposed acceptance probes. It prices Route A’s two applications, identity drift and offline adapter instead of pretending product adoption supplies offline automatically. It offers a one-server alternative, a SaaS alternative and explicit user choices. No whole obligation or explicit user constraint is omitted. Material defects in facts, ordinary custody flow and enforcement/validation remain despite that breadth.

axes.coverage: Complete relevant consequential primary review: products/identity/offline applicability, PostgreSQL ranges/predicates/locks, buffer and custody semantics, event history/CSV, three historical chains and version/deployment qualifications.
axes.judgment: The core PostgreSQL overlap example and per-key control-row fencing are source-grounded when their range and transaction premises hold. Units are explicit signed decimals per site; idempotency and offline capture/accept are separated. Audit bulk/raw caveats and pagination are supported. The LibreBooking API claim is wrong, and the custody/buffer backstops are materially incomplete. Grocy downstream symptoms are reports with credential-context exceptions, not proof of a universal endpoint removal. Invented seven-day/TTL/retention/RPO defaults are visibly design policy, not falsely sourced vendor defaults.

axes.coverage: Complete: every discovered family, retained option/condition, restored Snipe-IT option, qualified SaaS route, dropped OpenFab lead, Supabase/prototype seam.

The design distinguishes exclusive tools, copies and consumables and prices integrations. These are viable investigation paths under stated conditions, not demonstrated compatible deployments. OpenFab was properly removed rather than promoted from inadequate evidence. Supabase is a prototype backend proposal requiring a separate local store/outbox, not proof of built-in offline. Most useful option breadth survives; breadth does not excuse the source and mechanism defects.

plan_dispositions.candidate_disposition: CORRECTION; calendar view enhancement retained; quota/booking policy decisions; gap uncertainties
plan_dispositions.assessment: A shared calendar alone is not a complete makerspace inventory system, and reservation integrity must be explicit. The database-backed unique-resource route is reasonable. The candidate’s assertion that calendars categorically lack conflict handling is overbroad: Exchange resource mailboxes offer AutoAccept, AllowConflicts=false and recurrence conflict limits under documented mailbox/provisioning conditions. Existing licensing and offline support are unknown. This is a premise qualification, not evidence the exact calendar-only plan is adequate. Buffer enforcement is materially incomplete in the chosen final representation (N2-F03).

plan_dispositions.candidate_disposition: CORRECTION; barcode/low-stock enhancements; allow-negative policy decision
plan_dispositions.assessment: Replacing blind client absolute overwrites with per-site typed movements/idempotency/audit is a sound design option. A derived ledger still needs fenced checks, which M1 usefully supplies for a shared part/site. Mandatory no-row wording exceeds the evidence: transactionally updated stored balances with history are viable (InvenTree). The final does not show the same-site last-unit lock result applies across independent sites; V6 is wrong (N2-F04). Transfer policy and negative-stock exception are explicitly stated rather than sourced defaults.

plan_dispositions.candidate_disposition: CORRECTION; offline permit preserved; timestamps as evidence; queue/conflict policy decisions
plan_dispositions.assessment: Rejecting timestamp-only arbitration for scarce physical resources is justified: device skew and deterministic winners do not establish physical custody or fairness. The final retains offline intents, retries and capture/accept ordering, and explicitly chooses first-sync-wins with visible earlier capture and staff override. That is a declared product policy with fairness limits, not a factual claim that source code chooses the policy. TTL/outbox capacity and device loss are priced. The custody enforcement claimed to close the double-lend still lacks normal checkin release (N2-F02).

plan_dispositions.candidate_disposition: REJECT name overwrite; correction stable-key staged import; enhancements dry run/quarantine/mapping

Strings preserve leading zero IDs; file-level locale/delimiter and staff confirmation are sensible scoped policies. A file hash no-op rule is a deliberate import policy, not a universal correct reconciliation rule. Formula handling, uneven rows and correction reports are meaningful proposals awaiting runtime fixtures. Names remain hints, so user data can still assist matching without silent overwrite.

Cached status in Route A has a declared lag and staff-confirmation condition; the assessment does not treat a 15-minute cache as an instantly consistent safety guarantee. Most oracles discriminate real failures, while V6’s cross-site exactly-one criterion is wrong and the normal checkout/checkin/checkout flow exposes the incomplete custody model. criticism_adjudication.independent_adjudication: A concrete host/operator and outage tradeoff is useful. Nightly backup RPO and client outbox-loss limitations are stated, not claimed tested. The single-node tradeoff respects the brief rather than mandating enterprise failover. Hardware throughput, restore timings and device eviction remain honest build tests.

criticism_adjudication.candidate_response: ACCEPT: first-sync policy, expiry, loser workflow and device FIFO
criticism_adjudication.independent_adjudication: These were real policy holes, but public sync code cannot dictate the fair winner. The final makes first accepted server intent authoritative, preserves capture order for staff review, adds TTL and defines local FIFO scope. It acknowledges physical double-lend ambiguity and creates staff work rather than claiming a server can undo physical possession. This is a bounded product policy, not automatically proven fairness.

A server/database invariant for concurrent double checkout is well motivated. The final does not close the normal checkin release path under its append-only event declaration. The claimed complete closure is materially incomplete, even though a properly modeled open-state predicate could enforce one borrower.

criticism_adjudication.candidate_response: ACCEPT IDs; AMEND Chain 1 through issue/commit fetches
criticism_adjudication.independent_adjudication: Closing missing source IDs and retrieving the actual tall-view patch improves traceability. The patch genuinely concerns actual/buffered data and approximate end height. But #1220 is not proof of absent API implementation, and the linked merged #1235 expressly says support already existed with documentation missing. The claimed strengthened API chain is wrong.

Including completed historical rows is a declared audit/backdated-overlap policy, supported by partial exclusion semantics. It is not a PostgreSQL default. Cancellation/no-show and early completion semantics remain business policy.

Correctly distinguishes an earlier Supabase offline-adapter proposal from observed built-in offline prior art. Remote SDK/backend alone is not a local intent store; the proposed queue remains clearly additional architecture.

Narrowing a product assertion to the observed causal-history migration avoids turning the parts product into a proved repair-condition implementation. The independent PRs confirm new-write link then historical backfill.
Proper distinction between different files’ dialects and delimiters appearing inside quoted fields. Parser dialect detection does not authorize arbitrary row-level mixing.

Comparing independently recorded expected actions/actors/order links to audit entries is meaningful; it avoids merely checking an audit screen is nonempty. Bulk/raw bypass paths need either history helpers/logging or explicit prevention, as official history docs warn.
A pinned documented client contract and machine-readable status/body expectations can expose real auth/API breakage. It is a proposal, not proof of compatibility.
A per-file staff locale is a legitimate handling policy for ambiguous historical dates, not a parser fact. It preserves predictable parsing and quarantines genuinely unparseable values.
The official product source corroborates lending/reservation/member/site features more directly than a general tool-library secondary. Marketing capability is not offline/deployment proof.

criticism_adjudication.candidate_response: ACCEPT unsupported Open Fab Control removed
criticism_adjudication.independent_adjudication: Correctly drops an inadequately evidenced named option rather than fabricating an independent product finding. This does not prove the product cannot exist; the other relevant discovery paths remain.
Naming blocking versus degraded states resolves a real design ambiguity. These are maker policy defaults; available reference product status/history features support modeling, not these exact values.
The design states actor/reason, site movement and queue/due-state behavior. This is useful two-site semantics; multi-site products establish feasibility, not correctness of unexecuted transfer code.

Versioned REST, scoped tokens and at-least-once signed/retried webhooks with a dead-letter path are concrete design proposals. They remain a future integration contract needing execution; no fetched product API proves the candidate contract implemented.
The SQL mechanism is independently supported by version 18 docs. The candidate’s mutable /current/ reference is not an immutable release pin; this criticism is only partly closed.
Correct not to use the secondary example as governing evidence. The official range/exclusion sections directly substantiate the room/resource pattern and operator semantics.

Questioning invisible padding is sensible, but the final’s allowed buffer_minutes representation no longer participates in its shown range exclusion. The response preserves display clarity and loses the demonstrated concurrent enforcement relationship.

material_findings.title: A false compaction limit was introduced by accepting critic m7
material_findings.candidate_passage: compaction drops conflict bodies while keeping lineage … losing branches remain resolvable only within that bound
material_findings.original_obligation: Offline conflict/audit integrity; O2 compaction/revision exceptions; O5 independent adjudication of criticism

primary_evidence.version_or_locator: Apache CouchDB 3.5, §2.3.3/4, revision trees and resolving conflicts
Apache CouchDB issue #1507, historical design discussion; corroboration only

material_findings.reasoning: CouchDB 3.5 distinguishes current conflicting leaf revisions from old non-leaf history. Compaction discards bodies of non-leaf revisions, while current conflicting leaves remain available for explicit conflict resolution. _revs_limit bounds retained revision ancestry, not a time-to-live for every unresolved losing leaf. Historical ancestor bodies may be unavailable for a three-way merge and stemming can affect replication ancestry; those genuine caveats do not support the final’s blanket conflict-body/losing-branch expiry claim. The draft did not have this supposed operating bound; the critic introduced it and the final accepted and repeated it without primary support. It wrongly prices and limits the offline multi-master option and can misdirect retention decisions. This is not a claim that CouchDB revisions are an audit log or that purge/deletion cannot remove leaves.
material_findings.applicability: Applies to the actual final design/claim, with the stated source version and domain conditions; no candidate repair performed.

primary_evidence.version_or_locator: InvenTree StockItem.quantity/updateQuantity/add_stock/take_stock/lock_quantity; master accessed 2026-10-09; latest path commit 02da01dfec309ac410e846a57d329d0e96b90e21

material_findings.reasoning: Blind stale absolute overwrites really can lose updates and lack an audit trail. But the original P2 says a database row updated by each client; it does not state that clients bypass transactional server operations, share no location key, or erase a separate history. PostgreSQL Read Committed updates re-evaluate a concurrently changed target row, and a locked transactional increment/decrement with history can be safe. InvenTree itself has a stored Decimal StockItem.quantity; add_stock/take_stock use an atomic transaction, lock_quantity, updateQuantity and tracking entries. Thus the blanket assertion that the recommended reference products do not use such a stored quantity and the mandatory derived-only correction are not supported. A movement ledger is a useful proposed design, but the candidate turns that choice into a required correction by ruling out a demonstrably viable stored-balance-with-audit mechanism. This does not endorse direct offline LWW overwrites, and exact unit/location/negative-balance policy remains necessary.
material_findings.applicability: Applies to the actual final design/claim, with the stated source version and domain conditions; no candidate repair performed.

minor_findings.candidate_locator: line 23 and line 122 generic calendar rejection; Koha/OpenRoom rejection

Koha also has offline circulation/multi-branch support, though its ILS domain can make it a poor fit. These options require narrower fit reasoning; no evidence forces adoption or makes them an entire makerspace solution. OpenRoom repository lookup failed, which is not evidence of incapability.

PowerSync client re-sync validates a different loss surface from authoritative Postgres restoration; SaaS export is portability, not server recovery. The Postgres backup drill is stated separately under D. Criteria are proposed and their limitations should stay explicit.

The recommendation to test the common availability equation is well supported without that universal test-history assertion.

axes.coverage: Complete: O1–O6 and every explicit makerspace constraint, including staff workflow, unreliable two-site Wi-Fi, CSV, low hosting, double booking, audit and extensions.
axes.judgment: The final answers the original brief with an availability equation, explicit per-P fragments, several architecture paths, an honest executed/proposed split and design questions that depend on staff policy. A small single-writer backend and SaaS comparison respect the hosting constraint; offline identity and revocation are now explicit. All obligations have substantive content, and at least the Yale issue/patch chain satisfies the minimum evolution requirement. Material unsupported release/option claims and a false critic addition still prevent full quality.

axes.coverage: Complete relevant consequential primary review: availability/counting/TZ, transaction and replication semantics, revision exceptions, CSV config/error behavior, primary lending/stock products, operations and three evolution chains.
axes.judgment: Correct mechanisms include pairwise exclusion versus counted capacity, deterministic replication winners versus business arbitration, immediate versus eventual conflicts, parser data/errors/meta and true versus displayed availability. PowerSync’s backend arbitration is conservatively labeled inference and independently corroborated by official docs. The compaction bound is false, named PouchDB 9.0 Delta Sync/50% attribution lacks official release evidence, Turso versions are collapsed, and the universal derived-only quantity premise conflicts with actual InvenTree code. Small-binary memory figures and unpinned commercial adoption counts are insufficiently bounded minor claims, not benchmarked proof.

axes.coverage: Complete: all discovered tools/families, architecture A–F, explicit rejected options, optional leads and conditional hosting/offline tradeoffs.
axes.judgment: Circulate and YaleSTC are useful domain-specific discoveries; Snipe-IT, InvenTree and Grocy supply concrete custody/stock distinctions; PocketBase/SQLite/Litestream, CouchDB/PouchDB, PowerSync/Postgres and SaaS form genuinely different conditional options. Shelf and NocoDB/Baserow remain clearly uninvestigated leads. Domain-specific availability questions are a particular strength. Rejection of BOM/build depth and backup-as-sync is sensible. The Turso exclusion is not adequately version-grounded, and generic calendar/Koha dismissal needs narrower domain qualifications. No source-count ranking or requirement to adopt every possible product is applied.

axes.coverage: Complete: P1–P6 with all preserved fragments, optional enhancements, user decisions and externally unresolved items.
axes.judgment: The P1 reservation-source concern, P3 timestamp arbitration correction, P4 stable-key import, P5 repair gating and P6 expanded regressions are mostly well reasoned. P2 overcorrects by mandating derived-only quantities and making false generalized claims about row storage. Outlook/CalDAV calendar stores are not inherently incapable of resource reservations, but the brief still needs inventory/offline/audit functionality beyond a calendar. Optional enhancements and staff-dependent policies are labeled rather than smuggled into unconditional requirements.

axes.coverage: Complete: full stage comparison; M1–M4 and m1–m12 individually adjudicated, with D1–D8/U1–U6/R1–R3 and all alternatives/rejections tracked.
axes.judgment: The final preserves substantial prose and uncertainty, brings quantity, offline identity and membership interaction into the availability design, and prices validation by architecture. It correctly demotes an unverified cr-sqlite maintenance claim and keeps a new Airtable-class idea as a lead. Critic m7 is false and its acceptance introduces and propagates a false CouchDB limit. Critic M4’s blanket claim that SQLite concurrency is trivial is itself too strong; serializing writes does not automatically make an application’s stale read/check/write safe. The final’s transaction/serialized-winner criterion partly avoids that critic error. Critic agreement and the reviser’s read-only rechecks do not authenticate original secondary release claims.

axes.coverage: Complete: E1–E5 evidence/read-only witnesses versus proposed P-V1–P-V6, including each A–E architecture’s different oracle and recovery applicability.
axes.judgment: The candidate clearly says no runtime/reservation/import/recovery test ran. The capacity N+1→N case, both-versions staff arbitration, identity-revocation case, hostile CSV result taxonomy and availability matrix are meaningful. Different architecture criteria are useful, provided business success is not replaced by sync visibility or documenting a race. For PowerSync, rebuilding a client from Postgres does not test restoring the authoritative server; for SaaS, export is portability rather than server recovery. These are stated scope limits, not invented execution failure. Backup/restore performance, queue/retention bounds and deployment identity remain build validation.

grade_limits: FAIL is an independent source-grounded scientific grade after full six-axis artifact and consequential-claim review, not a delivery/native/cost grade.
No candidate runtime tests were executed; no failure or success rate, repair outcome, performance benchmark or deployed compatibility is inferred.
Honest staff/deployment inputs above are not counted as evasive missing research. Unsupported consequential claims are findings, not disguised unknown user decisions.
This is not comparative full quality: both arms have different strengths and defects, and two FAIL grades do not establish equivalence or a faster FAIL win.

plan_dispositions.candidate_disposition: CORRECTION; optional view/sync; D1 quantity/policy/TZ and D8 membership; uncertainty actual classes
plan_dispositions.assessment: The shared availability equation and count-versus-unit distinction improve the thin plan. Pairwise exclusion is not an aggregate capacity counter, and the per-unit/serializable/advisory-lock alternatives are stated rather than conflated. Date granularity, pending requests, overdue and admin overrides remain user choices informed by Yale, not imported Yale policies as requirements. The categorical rejection of Google/Outlook/CalDAV stores is too broad; resource-calendar processing can handle booking conflicts under specified configuration, though it does not supply the entire inventory/offline/audit solution.

plan_dispositions.candidate_disposition: CORRECTION; optional barcode; idempotency scope/window decisions; reorder uncertainty
plan_dispositions.assessment: The lost-update example is valid for stale absolute overwrites and a ledger/audit design is useful. The final’s mandatory derived-only architecture and claim that referenced products do not use a stored client-updated quantity are false as general statements (N1-F04). InvenTree provides a concrete locked, transactionally updated quantity plus history. Display-floor versus true quantity should remain separate; negative physical balance policy and per-location identity still require staff choices.

plan_dispositions.candidate_disposition: ALREADY-COVERED offline permit + CORRECTION reject timestamp reconciliation; D2 partition, D7 identity, bounded queues
plan_dispositions.assessment: The split is apt: unreliable sites need offline workflow but timestamps alone cannot resolve scarce custody. Immediate conflict retries versus eventual branches and both-version staff review are meaningful. Offline identity/revocation and queue overflow are surfaced rather than invented. Transport remains distinct from reservation arbitration. The newly accepted compaction expiry premise and named Delta Sync release performance are materially unsupported/wrong (N1-F01/F02); they do not invalidate the correctly scoped sync-versus-arbitration distinction.

plan_dispositions.candidate_disposition: CORRECTION reject names; stable IDs/dry-run/quarantine/undo; optional mapping memory; staff CSV choices
plan_dispositions.assessment: Sound preservation of names as possible hints rather than overwrite authority. Papa Parse data/errors/meta and FieldMismatch code handling support visible repair and string IDs. The final distinguishes a dict-header duplicate loss mechanism from the parser’s specific behavior; current Papa docs automatically rename duplicates and expose renamedHeaders, so do not assume Papa itself silently overwrites. Explicit export quoting/newline settings are useful proposals.

plan_dispositions.candidate_disposition: CORRECTION notes-only; retain text in repair case; optional photo/parts/reminders; repair lifecycle decisions
plan_dispositions.assessment: Repair cases/history and availability gating serve the staff workflow better than a free-text-only flag. The final does not discard free text. Member-facing reminders are a future seam rather than an unconditional new v1 requirement. State/booking interaction is made part of the common availability matrix. Cross-site conflict handling for a repair race remains a proposed fixture, not source-proven behavior.

plan_dispositions.candidate_disposition: CORRECTION expand beyond happy path; already-covered normal flows retained; architecture-priced probes
plan_dispositions.assessment: Expanded tests address actual availability failures, partitions, identity, hostile CSV, repair/audit and recovery. Architecture-specific success conditions are valuable. SQLite still needs a correct transaction around the decision; write serialization alone does not justify calling a concurrency test trivial. P-V5 scopes are different: client re-sync and SaaS export are not equivalent to authoritative-server disaster recovery. They are openly proposed and no runtime witness is fabricated.

criticism_adjudication.independent_adjudication: Real omission: pairwise per-tool exclusion does not express arbitrary at-most-N capacity. Per-unit assignment plus exclusion or a correctly serialized counted guard are legitimate design options. The added N+1 versus N test and equation row are meaningful, with architecture-specific transaction validation still required.

criticism_adjudication.candidate_response: ACCEPT explicit offline identity decision and test
criticism_adjudication.independent_adjudication: Actor-dependent events require an identity policy under partition; sync visibility is not identity acquisition. D7 surfaces options and a revoked/lapsed actor review case without inventing the actual staff mechanism. Proportionate to the brief; not a demand for a specific identity product.

criticism_adjudication.candidate_response: ACCEPT with AMEND recommended membership default
criticism_adjudication.independent_adjudication: A stated member eligibility/lifecycle interaction is useful. The critic’s particular membership default is not dictated by public lending products. Final D8 explicitly permits staff confirmation and even no v1 lifecycle. This preserves uncertainty rather than importing requirements from a reference system.

Different A–E failure surfaces warrant different criteria. But the critic/final statement that concurrency is trivial under a single SQLite writer is too strong: serialization of writes does not prevent an application from making a stale precheck outside its apply transaction. The final’s serialized ledger-winner and transaction-oriented criteria are a better bounded reading. P-V5 client re-sync/export have narrower oracles than authoritative recovery.

criticism_adjudication.candidate_response: ACCEPT secondary room example, defer build pin
criticism_adjudication.independent_adjudication: Official PostgreSQL §8.17.10 directly supplies a room/range exclusion example. The range mechanism is supported now, not merely by agreement among snippets. The final’s pin deferral is a minor reproducibility issue, not reason to reject the mechanism.

criticism_adjudication.candidate_response: ACCEPT downgrade unverified cr-sqlite maintenance premise
criticism_adjudication.independent_adjudication: Dropping a secondary maintenance assertion is correct. Rejecting silent auto-merge as a scarce-resource arbiter is a scoped design reason; it does not reject every CRDT use. Current source describes CRDT/causal-log mechanics, not a magical physical-custody oracle.

criticism_adjudication.independent_adjudication: The prior fetched visibility/sync-rules docs did not establish the arbitration mechanism. Honest inference labeling is appropriate. Independent official conflict docs now corroborate backend-defined conflict handling and upload operation semantics, so this is a sound conditional conclusion, not a false correction.

They also reveal disabled specs and a later overdue-flag problem. Snippet convergence alone was never primary validation; the equation lesson stands on the retrieved records.

criticism_adjudication.candidate_response: ACCEPT CSV commit as snippet illustration
criticism_adjudication.independent_adjudication: Independent complete relevant patches of 36f7dc5 confirm structured CSV result/error handling and the viewer surface. Papa Parse’s primary data/errors/meta and FieldMismatch taxonomy support the core import rule. The candidate correctly does not claim to have executed the importer or fetched the diff.

Reject the critic premise: it conflates compacted non-leaf historical bodies with current conflicting leaves. The final’s new losing-branch expiry bound is materially wrong and propagated into B and the conditions. Independent evidence, not acceptance by the reviser, governs.
Papa Parse docs support explicit newline/quote configuration and CRLF defaults. Naming export settings is a sensible extension to retained report/export scope, not an executed portability result.

Correctly retained as an uninvestigated lead with no asserted mechanism and no changed P disposition. It would enrich O1 if pursued; the original brief does not mandate exhaustive product discovery or a repair of this optional lead.
evidence: N1 final line 121 and stage comparison

criticism_adjudication.candidate_response: ACCEPT member-facing reminders as future seam
criticism_adjudication.independent_adjudication: Member communication is plausibly supported by official lending-product features. Final labels due/overdue notices a future seam rather than an unconditional v1 implementation burden.

Explicit retention/overflow design requirements are useful. No source bounds this makerspace’s outage/storage needs, so not inventing N days is appropriate. This is an unresolved design parameter, not failure to fetch an available numerical answer.

Intent UUID shape and dedup scope/window are explicit implementation decisions. Official backend-sync guidance supports idempotent operation handling. The final does not pretend that an unstated lifetime is a source default or a tested guarantee.

Do not accept blanket concurrence: stored quantity rows have supported safe forms, m7 introduces a false operating premise, and the broad Turso rejection lacks version applicability. General calendar fit also needs qualification. Most retained narrower roles and explicit uncertain decisions are sound.

method_clues: N2 paths disclose control; N1 paths disclose treatment and M10 question queues. Stage assignments/source indexes disclose methods and claimed native IDs. Partial blinding only. No candidate history, other cases, evaluator answers or private provider internals were accessed. Citation count, method label, apparent agreement and file length did not determine grades.
scope_limits: Both complete frozen finals, discoveries, drafts, critiques, source maps, source-root excerpts/indexes, stage assignments/input maps and plan-reveal records were read. All declared SHA-256 and byte sizes match the exact evaluation input-map.

Relevant public primary documentation, releases, issue/PR bodies and patches were independently retrieved. Candidate secondary claims were checked against primaries or classified unsupported; honest deployment/user unknowns remain unknown.

No candidate application, PostgreSQL, CouchDB, PouchDB, importer or recovery drill was executed. Proposed test designs and their oracles were assessed; static semantic traces are reasoning aids, not runtime proof.

Public current/master sources can drift. Historical claims were checked with named releases/commits when available; current documentation does not prove a deployment release or the makerspace’s operating policies.

The assessment does not demand an unlimited production specification, every possible product, or invented workload/budget/policy answers. Optional uninvestigated leads remain optional, not missing required facts.

independent_synthesis: Both arms offer useful but different work. N2 is more concrete about a product-adoption route, lifecycle defaults and custody/stock operations, but its stated backstops and one test oracle have concrete holes. N1 is stronger in the lending availability equation, counted capacity and architecture-specific testing, but accepts a false critic compaction premise and makes unsupported release/option and overbroad stock-storage claims. These observations do not yield a full-quality ranking, equal quality, or a speed win; comparative_quality_eligible is false.
